annotations.text:
This is the page to judge, and judging it means looking at it on the monitor you actually work on — not on this one, at this brightness.

Every hex here is now normative: design_tokens.md §10.4 carries the four-step ladder, the text ramp, and both severity columns. Every pair is contrast-checked and every L* figure is computed. Two values were replaced during derivation: muted text failed at 4.35:1 on the raised surface, and a border that carries meaning has to be far lighter than intuition suggests — #5E6B7A, where the first three candidates all failed 3:1.

The ground is #0E141B, L* 6.1. It is deliberately not black: below roughly L* 5 near-white text starts to bloom, which costs sharpness rather than adding it. The diagnostic canvas is #0A0C0E in both themes, deliberately not the chrome navy.

Contrast ratios are necessary, not sufficient. If this reads wrong in the room, the values change regardless of what the arithmetic says.

Light mode is now the override, not the default — D-013 has the app open dark whatever the OS says, on the reasoning that a system preference is set for a different room.

These three were drawn before that decision, so read them as the light-mode treatment of the same screens rather than as the app's front door. The layout, hierarchy and type decisions carry over unchanged; only the palette swaps.

This graph is a proposal, not a record. The app has no runtime navigation at all — seven routes, zero edges.
The three amber cards call out the decisions worth arguing with.

Three of these designs are currently asserted as WRONG by passing tests, so building them means changing tests too:
• the severity dot is pinned to a circle
• the heatmap canvas is pinned to the chrome navy
• the auth card is pinned to an overlay shadow

The severity silhouettes are new — nothing in the app draws an icon for severity today. The Appearance control now starts on Dark, per D-013.

The compact tier from design_tokens.md §9.5 — under 600px, drawn dark since that's the default now (D-013). This also closes part of the dark-coverage gap: Chat and the worklist previously existed only in light.

Following §9.5 to the letter, not improvising: conversations collapse to an overlay drawer (try the menu button on Chat — phone); findings become a persistent bottom sheet that keeps the critical count on screen even while typing; the heatmap goes full-bleed with controls over a scrim, discrete opacity stops instead of a continuous slider so every stop is its own 44px target (try it).

No painted status bar or keyboard on any of these — the real device draws its own, and a fake one doubles up. Five new pairs this page introduces (icon labels on the diagnostic canvas, button text on the accent fill, secondary text on the brand surfaces, severity-as-border) are all contrast-checked; none reuse an unverified guess.

Still missing at this width: Settings, Login, Onboarding — none of the three exist at any size yet.
